profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Morse Road Southwest, Pataskala, Jersey Township, Licking County, OH 43062
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's New Albany-area, Ohio data center footprint, mapped on Morse Road Southwest in Pataskala, Jersey Township, Licking County, and carries the informational label NBY-7 in this registry's underlying mapping data, not independently confirmed against a Google-published building index this session. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within this footprint.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

Ohio's central corridor data center cluster, of which this Licking County building is part, has grown rapidly since 2019 alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Ohio footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google has not published the power capacity, square footage, or building-level details for NBY-7, following its standard disclosure policy of reporting only aggregate figures at the state level. This facility is part of a multi-county Columbus-area campus that received $1.7 billion in announced investment alongside a reported $600 million for the initial New Albany site, placing Google among the largest hyperscale operators in the Licking County corridor alongside AWS and Meta.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 operators have published power figures totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity across the state. NBY-7 does not contribute to this published total and therefore cannot be ranked against other Ohio facilities by disclosed power.

Without published specifications, NBY-7 cannot be evaluated for its direct relevance to AI scaling in terms of power delivery, rack density, or cooling architecture. The scale of Google's regional investment and its choice to develop in Licking County alongside competing hyperscalers suggests strategic importance to the operator, but individual facility capabilities remain opaque.
